+

+set_option autoImplicit false

+/-- The first-quadrant Cech double complex of an arbitrary module complex,
+with resolution degree first. This extends moduleCechDouble to acyclic resolutions.
+Source: Stacks Project, Tag 01EQ.
+(blueprint: def-sc-cech-cup-resolution-comparison-data) -/
+def cupCechDouble {X : Scheme.{v}} {ι : Type v} (U : ι → X.Opens)
+    (K : CochainComplex X.Modules ℕ) :
+    HomologicalComplex₂ (ModuleCat.{v} Γ(X, ⊤)) (ComplexShape.up ℕ) (ComplexShape.up ℕ) :=
+  ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
+      PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op ⋙
+        cechComplexFunctor U).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj K
+
+/-- Alpha, beta and the computing identification for an acyclic resolution.
+The component equations specify the actual restriction and augmentation maps.
+The class equations identify them with the canonical injective comparisons.
+Source: Stacks Project, Tags 01EQ and 0FKV.
+(blueprint: def-sc-cech-cup-resolution-comparison-data) -/
+structure CupCechResolutionComparison {X : Scheme.{v}} {ι : Type v}
+    (U : ι → X.Opens) {F : X.Modules} (D : CupAcyclicResolution F) where
+  alpha : ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
+    (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.K ⟶ (cupCechDouble U D.K).total (ComplexShape.up ℕ)
+  beta : (cechComplexFunctor U).obj F.presheafModuleCat ⟶
+    (cupCechDouble U D.K).total (ComplexShape.up ℕ)
+  alpha_f : ∀ n : ℕ, alpha.f n = moduleCechZero U (D.K.X n) ≫
+    (cupCechDouble U D.K).ιTotal (ComplexShape.up ℕ) n 0 n (by simp)
+  beta_f : ∀ n : ℕ, beta.f n =
+    ((cechComplexFunctor U).map
+      ((PresheafOfModules.forgetToPresheafModuleCat (op ⊤) isTerminalTop.op).map
+        (D.augmentation.f 0).val)).f n ≫
+      (cupCechDouble U D.K).ιTotal (ComplexShape.up ℕ) 0 n n (by simp)
+  alpha_quasiIso : QuasiIso alpha
+  iso : ∀ n : ℕ, (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace n).obj F ≅
+    ((cupCechDouble U D.K).total (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).homology n
+  alpha_class : ∀ (n : ℕ)
+    (z : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
+      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.K).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
+    (iso n).hom (D.class n z) =
+      HomologicalComplex.homologyMap alpha n (cupCycleClass _ n z)
+  beta_class : ∀ (n : ℕ)
+    (c : ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj F.presheafModuleCat).homology n ⟶
+      (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace n).obj F),
+    IsModuleCechComparison U F n c →
+    ∀ z : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj F.presheafModuleCat).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K,
+      (iso n).hom (c (cupCycleClass _ n z)) =
+        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap beta n (cupCycleClass _ n z)

+end
+end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules

+/-! # Existence of Cech comparisons for a computing resolution pairing
+
+Source: Stacks Project, Tags 01EQ and 0FKV.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+universe v
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
+set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency.types false
+open CategoryTheory CategoryTheory.Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace

+/-- A computing sectionwise resolution pairing admits canonical Cech comparison
+maps. This supplies only alpha, beta and their identifications, not a cup comparison.
+Source: Stacks Project, Tag 0FKV, proof of Lemma 20.31.4, flasque-resolution paragraph;
+Tag 01EQ, proof of the canonical Cech comparison.
+(blueprint: lem-sc-cech-cup-resolution-comparison-exists)
+
+Proof: take nonnegative Godement/flasque resolutions of F, G and F tensor G with
+their augmentation-preserving section pairing. Compare them to injective resolutions
+over the coefficient augmentations; flasque acyclicity makes the comparisons compute
+global cohomology and thus supplies CupResolutionPairing D. For each of its three
+resolutions use restriction to Cech degree zero for alpha, and augmentation into
+resolution degree zero for beta. Naturality of restriction and the zero differential
+of the augmentation verify their cochain identities. Flasque Cech acyclicity and the
+first-quadrant column comparison show alpha is a quasi-isomorphism. Define iso by the
+inverse of the resolution's computing global comparison, the injective-resolution
+cohomology identification, and H(alpha). This gives alpha_class. Map the entire Cech
+double complex to the one for the injective resolution. Its alpha and beta squares
+commute by naturality and the over-augmentation equality. The injective alpha map is
+a quasi-isomorphism; cancellation in these squares and IsModuleCechComparison give
+beta_class for every specified canonical comparison. Degree zero and an empty cover
+of the empty scheme use the same cochain identities and require no exception. -/
+theorem exists_cupCechResolutionComparison (X : Scheme.{v}) {ι : Type v}
+    (U : ι → X.Opens) (hU : iSup U = ⊤) (F G : X.Modules) :
+    ∃ D : CupResolutionPairing F G,
+      Nonempty (CupCechResolutionComparison U D.left) ∧
+      Nonempty (CupCechResolutionComparison U D.right) ∧
+      Nonempty (CupCechResolutionComparison U D.target) := by sorry
+
+end
+end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules

+Proof: on the summand with resolution/Cech bidegrees (r,i) and (s,j), restrict the
+first factor to the front i+1 vertices and the second to the last j+1 vertices,
+apply D.pair r s on their common intersection, and multiply by (-1)^(i*s).
+Include the resulting section in bidegree (r+s,i+j) of the target total complex.
+Finite direct-sum assembly and bilinearity give the map from the tensor of total
+complexes. The Cech Leibniz identity follows by adjacent omitted-vertex cancellation;
+the resolution Leibniz identity is D.leibniz. The displayed sign makes these agree
+with the total differentials, so the map is a cochain pairing and descends to the
+bilinear map t on homology: the Leibniz identity pairs cycles to cycles and pairs
+a boundary with a cycle to a boundary in either factor, so quotient descent is
+well-defined. On alpha images i=j=0: the sign is one and restriction
+compatibility of D.pair gives the first square. On beta images r=s=0: again the

+axis inclusions. Pass both equalities to homology to get the two asserted cycle

+is used in this step. -/
